changelog.summary: Fixed The Casting loading as unstyled text with no photos when opened from this site -- its stylesheets, scripts and photo data live as separate files and were being looked for on the wrong site, so none of them arrived. Renamed "The Fracture Everywhere" to just "The Fracture" everywhere it appears, and folded in the older "All Fracture" name that was still showing on several pages, so there is now one name. New cover art for The Festie Codex.

Added real commissioned cover art for The Loop, The Weighing, and The Festie Bible, and a new hero image for The Casting, replacing placeholder icons. Fixed hero stat counts that had drifted stale (said 8 books/2 tools/2 craft lines against an actual 9/3/3) and completed the footer's Library and Workshop link lists, which were each missing several entries. Deployed live via the Netlify MCP deploy tool (confirmed working in this environment after earlier incorrectly reporting no deploy capability).

The Festie Bible's address (/festival) is now actually live and working -- fixed a JavaScript syntax error (smart/curly quotes used as real code delimiters) and a missing data declaration that both black-screened the book on entry. Added The Casting to the Workshop: a new card linking to the eco-resin/candle/glow-art site at /resin.

Added The Festie Bible as a new book in the Library -- twelve field guides for every corner of the festival world (women, men, first-timers, LGBTQ+ attendees, artists, musicians, vendors, staff, harm reduction, camp leads, promoters, health & safety). Not fully live yet -- the book itself is built, but its own address is still pending a hosting decision.

The opening walkthrough is now a real guided tour -- it lights up one door at a time and tells you what is behind that one, then points out the coin and the music button, instead of dumping all five things into a single block of text. You can still tap a door at any point to skip ahead. Fixed the intro video cutting out after about three seconds: when a phone refuses to autoplay (Low Power Mode does this), the opening frame now holds as a title card you can tap to actually watch the clip, rather than giving up and fading away. The last two links still pointing at a raw netlify.app address -- The Portals and The Press -- now use noblefathercreations.com/portals and /press like everything else.

The corner button is now the actual Noble Father mark (a coin, not a generic icon). Music is back -- it starts softly once you choose a door, with a new button next to it to mute it any time. The tutorial now explains both buttons. Fixed every link on the page that was sending people to a bare netlify.app address instead of noblefathercreations.com/faith, /playbook, and the rest -- those addresses were never actually wired up before, so this is the first time they work.

The red button in the corner is now the Noble Father mark instead of the letters "NF". Fixed the title being sliced in half at the top of the opening screen: the door screen had more on it than fits a phone, so it had been scrolling inside its own frame. It now shows only what an entrance needs -- the mark, the title, one line, and the three doors -- and fits one screen on every phone, tablet and laptop, with the rest of the page returning the moment a door is chosen. "The Workshop" no longer wraps onto a second line under its door, and the last words of the link below the doors no longer hide behind the corner button. Visitors who have motion turned down, and phones in Low Power Mode (which blocks video outright), now get the opening frame held as a still title card instead of a blank screen, and the rest of the page keeps its gentle fades instead of switching off every animation.

A pass on the small stuff that adds up: every button and card now visibly presses when tapped or clicked, not just when hovered -- including the tutorial's own "Choose a door" button, which previously had no reaction to a click at all. Fixed a touch-device bug where the 3D book-tilt effect in the Library and Workshop could stay stuck in its tilted position after tapping a card, since phones fake a hover state on tap; it's now a real mouse-only effect with its own separate tap feedback. The four opening numbers (2 living tools, 8 books, and so on) now count in one after another instead of appearing all at once.

Fixed the intro video not playing and the tutorial not appearing on some phones; the 3 doors are now genuinely the only thing you can do until you pick one (scrolling past them no longer works); each door now visibly moves instead of only reacting to hover, which never fires on a touch screen. Also found and fixed a layout bug this same round introduced -- the door screen had grown taller than one view, and centering it on the doors pushed the title off the top of the screen with no way to scroll back to it; it now scrolls smoothly within its own frame instead. Typography rebuilt: the display serif now uses its full character at large sizes, headings have real weight contrast, and small print moved out of the monospace into something easier to read on a phone.

projects.title: The Festie Bible
projects.tagline: Twelve field guides for the whole festival world
projects.localSourceNote: 2026-08-10: built from the 183-page FestieBible COMPLETE COLLECTION PDF (3 files, 60+61+62 pages) the user uploaded. Content extracted via OCR (the source PDF has broken font ligature mappings that silently drop letters from its own text stream -- OCR against the 300dpi render was used as ground truth instead) into content/festie-bible-data.json (12 guides, 149 scenarios, ~44k words of scenario prose). Rebuilt as a single self-contained HTML app (data-driven template, not hand-typed pages) using the hub design tokens (Fraunces/Hanken Grotesk/Space Mono, warm plum-black + brass palette) plus a 12-color persona accent per guide. Linked from the hub Library as VOL. X. NOT YET DEPLOYED -- needs a new Netlify site (or another hosting decision) before /festiebible resolves; see _redirects TODO in noble-father-catalogue._redirects. 2026-08-10 (later): deployed live at noble-festie-bible.netlify.app, routed through noblefathercreations.com/festival via _redirects. Prior to deploy, a design/UI review agent found the scenario data had severe, systemic extraction corruption (check-field bleed and MOVE/SAY/TRUTH column-header text glued onto ~145/149 scenarios, OCR glyph misreads of capital I as !/⁄/|/l, ~30 truncated hook titles, a leaked © bullet-glyph artifact, trailing page-marker fragments, and assorted missing-space typos) -- fixed across four review rounds, each verified against the raw OCR text and re-scanned with a full-dataset regex/structural/tokenization sweep before the corruption was confirmed fully resolved.

changelog.summary: Added a way out of the book: a House link in the top bar on every page and a link to the rest of the catalogue in the footer. Previously the only links out were TikTok, email and the crisis resources, so the only way back was the browser's back button.

Redesigned the homepage: the 314-word mission statement used to fill the entire first screen before the twelve guides appeared -- it now sits in its own readable section further down, broken into paragraphs, and the guide grid shows up right away. Added polish throughout: proper press feedback on every button/link that was missing it, a staggered entrance for guide cards and scenario-index lists, and named-property transitions in place of the one remaining catch-all transition. Deployed live.

Editorial prose polish across all 149 scenarios (12 guides) -- fixed 46 unbalanced quotation marks, 12 stray parser-artifact fragments, 5 remaining glued darkTitle/dark pairs, and ~20 scattered typos. Not a rewrite -- the prose was already strong; this was a precision cleanup pass. Deployed live.

Fixed a black-screen bug on entering any guide: curly/smart quotes had corrupted the JavaScript in renderGuideIntro() (used as real code delimiters, not just apostrophes) and the SCENARIO_INDEX data block had gone missing entirely during an earlier data fix. Also added a per-guide scenario navigation index so every scenario in a guide is one tap away from its intro page, instead of only reachable by paging through sequentially. Verified live via curl + node --check against the deployed file, not just the local copy.

Increased font sizes across the app for readability, fixed a sticky-bar/footer overlap bug, wired up the previously-unused footer/colophon, and fixed systemic scenario-data extraction corruption found by review (garbled check callouts, mislabeled Move/Say/Truth text, truncated titles, and various typos across most of the 149 scenarios). Deployed live.

First build. All 12 guides (G.R.O.V.E./B.A.S.S./R.A.V.E./P.R.I.D.E./C.R.E.A.T.E./S.O.U.N.D./M.A.R.K.E.T./H.O.L.D./C.A.R.E./L.E.A.D./E.V.E.N.T./S.A.F.E.), 149 scenario pages, extracted and rebuilt with a real logo (the source PDF's brand mark rendered at ~10% opacity -- fixed), reading-progress bar, in-guide contents drawer, and a persistent crisis-resource strip.

changelog.summary: Added the final inventory batch: 133 new pieces, taking the collection from 293 to 426. Every new piece was photographed, auto-cropped, colour-corrected and filed by subject, type and finish. Most of this batch is unpainted white resin, so you can now browse blanks as well as finished pieces. Tag list cut from 126 to 42 -- narrow one-offs folded into broader groups so filtering is actually usable. Also fixed three photos where the auto-crop had locked onto the backdrop instead of the (white) statue and cropped the piece out of frame, and corrected the Portals link so it works from either address.

Mobile: the filter panel (subject/type/finish/tag chips) no longer renders fully open by default -- it's collapsed behind a Filters button, so the product grid is visible without scrolling past the whole taxonomy first. Added press feedback (a small tap animation) to every button, chip, and link that was missing it. The piece viewer now opens with an animation that zooms in from the photo you tapped, instead of just from the center of the screen. Grid tiles fade in with a slight stagger instead of all at once. Fixed a leftover 'Untitled piece' placeholder that could show up in the viewer. Deployed live.

Deeper tag cleanup (146 unique tags, down from 235) and moved the project into its own git repo so it can be edited going forward. NOTE: the tag cleanup is committed to the new repo but NOT yet redeployed live -- Netlify account hit its usage/credit cap mid-deploy ('Skipped due to account credit usage exceeded'). Live site still shows the v2 pass (235 tags) until redeployed.
Fixed color tags (removed), duplicate tags (merged), false uniqueness claims (corrected), and a sticky filters panel that could obstruct the whole gallery. Deployed live.
